title: Interaction Budgeting — rough PRD and experiment notes
content:
Context / motivation:
We get repeated asks from product teams to support finer-grained token / latency budgeting per user session so that (a) heavy-power users don’t blow spend unexpectedly and (b) we can gracefully degrade fidelity when customers hit their soft caps. Redwood has batching, KV caching, and tiered model variants — this is about wiring a developer-first surface that maps business rules -> runtime policies.

Goal (high-level):
- Provide an opt-in "interaction budget" feature that:
  * lets apps declare a per-session token or cost budget (soft/hard),
  * exposes clear signals to the runtime to degrade fidelity or switch model variants when budget thresholds are hit,
  * surfaces telemetry and user-visible reason codes for degraded responses.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to design accounting for multi-tenant billing reconciliation (finance will need separate hook).
- Not building an auto-charge / upsell flow — that's downstream.

User personas:
- Growth PM: wants predictable monthly spend and a way to throttle power-users.
- Platform engineer: wants deterministic latency guarantees for premium routes while best-effort on cheap tiers.
- Product engineer (client): wants a simple API to attach an interaction budget to a session and get back reasons/metadata when degraded.

Examples of developer UX:
- Create session with budget: POST /v1/sessions { budget_tokens: 2000, budget_mode: "soft" }
- On responses: runtime returns headers: x-budget-remaining, x-budget-state=[OK|SOFT_EXCEEDED|HARD_EXCEEDED], x-budget-action=[none|compress|switch-model|trim-history]
- Webhook/telemetry for budget events: /budget-events callback when crossing thresholds.

User stories (rough):
1) As a product engineer I can create a session with a token budget and see the remaining budget on each response so I can show a progress bar in the client.
   - acceptance: header present + values in telemetry events.
2) As an API user I can choose soft vs hard budgets; soft triggers progressive fidelity policies while hard stops generation when exceeded.
   - acceptance: soft budgets allow fallback strategies; hard budgets return error/403-like termination responses for subsequent calls.
3) As an ops engineer I can configure default fidelity policies per customer tier (e.g., premium=no compression, standard=compress after 70% spend).
   - acceptance: console UI stubs + API to set routing policy present.

Policy primitives (runtime hooks):
- budget_remaining (tokens / estimated cost)
- thresholds: warn_at, degrade_at, halt_at (percent or absolute)
- actions: compress-history(n), prefer-llm-quantized, switch-model(to: compatible-compact), truncate-prefix(keep-last-k-turns), deny-request
- reason codes for debugging: BGT_WARN, BGT_DEGRADE, BGT_HALTED

Telemetry / observability:
- Per-session: initial_budget, current_remaining, cumulative_tokens_generated, list of actions applied + timestamps.
- Console: per-customer distribution of budget hits, top reasons, cost saved by compression policies.
- Alerts: >5% sessions hitting HARD within a deployment window -> paging.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: session create + headers implemented (minimal schema)
- Runtime: honor one simple policy (when remaining < X% -> switch to model-compact)
- Telemetry: events emitted and console table with top-level counts
- SDK: JS helper that reads X headers and emits events to client (open-source snippet)

Metrics to track:
- % sessions with budgets defined (adoption)
- % sessions that hit soft / hard thresholds
- avg tokens saved per degraded session
- user-visible latency change after degradation
- negative signal: drop in user satisfaction (NPS / direct feedback) by cohort

Experiment matrix (quick ideas):
- A/B: baseline (no budgeting) vs budgeting soft-compress policy -> measure per-session cost change and retention metrics.
- Per-workload policy: docs summarization vs chat assistant (where compression hurts relevance).

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal alpha for 2 product teams (console + APIs) — manual guardrails, feature flags.
2) Beta with limited customers + default conservative policies.
3) GA: enable via console + templates for common workloads.

Risks and mitigation:
- Over-aggressive compression could regress quality: mitigation = conservative defaults + per-prompt eval hooks.
- Complexity in mapping tokens to cost across quantized/compact models: mitigation = expose "estimated_cost_units" and normalize using model price table.
- Customer confusion: provide clear docs + example UX + recommended templates per workload.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- How do we handle multi-turn systems where the model needs earlier context for correctness? (Idea: weighted retention where last k turns always kept, earlier turns compressed into summary)
- Does Dedicated / Private need different semantics (likely yes: local admin controls)?
- Billing semantics: how does budget map to invoiceable usage when customers later disable budgeting? Need finance input.
- Product: do we surface spend progress to end-users (privacy / UX considerations)?
- Engineering: storage/lookup cost for per-session bookkeeping at scale — can we piggyback on existing session-store?

Implementation notes (starter tech design):
- Session object in session-store: { id, start_ts, initial_budget_units, remaining_units, policy_ref }
- At response emission, runtime deducts estimated cost and emits budget event to event-log (kafka)
- Policy engine: simple rule-evaluator (json-based) living in the routing layer. Start with deterministic rules, later add ML-driven suggestions in Optimize.

Short-term todo list (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Proto for session API + example SDK headers (JS)
- [ ] Small runtime hook to read remaining budget and apply model switch when below threshold (P0)
- [ ] Quick console table mockup for team review
- [ ] Write 5 prompt-based evals to test quality after compression/switch for chat and summarization flows

Notes for later / other features:
- "Budget pooling" across family of sessions (e.g., team-level quota)
- Auto-top-up / upsell suggestion flow in console when customers repeatedly hit hard caps
- Intelligent summarization lens that rewrites old context into condensed memory objects (Optimize integration)

Random brainstorm bullets (low fidelity):
- budget as non-linear: early tokens cost less to preserve onboarding quality, later tokens more heavily penalized
- visual SDK: progress meter with color thresholds + suggestion chips ("trim history" button)

End-of-file — Keaton notes: this should be minimal-first MVP, don't try to solve billing here. Focus on a clear API, deterministic runtime policy, and measurable telemetries.
